sources.entry: vulture - A tool for finding and analyzing dead Python code.

summary.one_liner: Vulture is a static analysis tool that finds unused (dead) code in Python programs by parsing their ASTs.
summary.what_it_does: Vulture scans Python files and directories and reports unused functions, classes, methods, attributes, variables, imports, and unreachable code. It uses the ast module to record defined and used names and reports objects that are defined but never referenced, ignoring scopes. Each finding gets a confidence value from 60% to 100%, and --min-confidence filters results. It can sort findings by size with --sort-by-size. False positives can be suppressed with whitelist modules (--make-whitelist), --exclude, --ignore-names, --ignore-decorators, underscore-prefixed names, or noqa comments for F401 and F841. Settings can be stored in pyproject.toml under [tool.vulture]. It also exposes a Python API (vulture.Vulture().scavenge() and get_unused_code()).
use_cases: find unused functions and classes in a Python project
locate untested code by running on library and test suite
clean up dead code before a release
run dead-code checks in a pre-commit hook
reduce false positives with whitelist files
notable: Confidence scores per finding type (100% for unused arguments and unreachable code, 90% for imports, 60% for functions, classes, attributes and variables)
Whitelist approach: a Python module that simulates usage, which can be auto-generated with --make-whitelist
Configurable through pyproject.toml, with command-line options taking precedence
Detects unreachable code after return, break, continue, raise and unsatisfiable if/while conditions
Pre-commit hook and programmatic API support
caveats: Static analysis misses dynamically called code, so some reported code is a false positive; values below 100% are rough estimates
Ignores scopes and only matches object names
Requires whitelists or ignore options to handle framework-invoked code such as decorated routes
keywords: check for dead code in my project
